approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would authorise the remaining spending for the Parliamentary Departments for the 2025-2026 financial year.
It would draw money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to cover the last seven months of the year, from December 2025 to June 2026.
The bill is a reintroduction of a lapsed version and includes an $800 million saving from reduced spending on consultants, contractors, labour hire, and non-wage expenses.
Proposes appropriations from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the Parliamentary Departments.
Provides the remaining 7/12ths of estimated 2025-26 annual appropriations.
Reflects an $800 million saving in 2025-26 from cutting spending on consultants, contractors, labour hire, and non-wage expenses.

Moved that the bill be read a second time, seeking $14.6 billion from the Consolidated Revenue Fund and total funding of $25.5 billion for non-ordinary annual government services in 2025-26. Reported funding for Defence, infrastructure, transport and finance, including the Inland Rail program, NBN fibre upgrades and support for the first-ever Hindu school in Australia.

Supported the appropriation bills to ensure continuity of government services but argued that the government's economic management had weakened living standards, increased spending, debt and taxes, and failed to grow productivity; he called for fiscal rules to contain spending.

Declared that Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026, Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2025-2026 and Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026 stood referred to the Federation Chamber for further debate.
Returned Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026, Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2025-2026 and Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026 to the House for further consideration.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders to set expedited proceedings and portfolio timeframes for the appropriation bills, require questions to be put without debate at specified stages, and allow variations only on a motion moved by a Minister.
